comment: Zero clue why AR has any bad ratings! I came into this class as a bio major who has never been a fan of Shakespeare, but he taught the course with such passion and joy that I couldn't help but learn to love it. He's also incredibly intelligent and made the texts so interesting. One of my favorite profs I've had, highly highly recommend to anyone!!!

Professor Russell is an AMAZING professor! There is a lot of reading, but it's worth it because the class discussions are very engaging. You can tell he loves teaching and has a passion for literature. He has high expectations for essays, but he is always willing to meet outside of class to help. Highly recommend!

I have no idea why he has some low ratings. Dr. Russell was by far the BEST professor that I have had at Richmond. He is very intelligent and helps you really understand Shakespeare. He made that class fun and rather easy.

Russell is easily one of the best professors here, he's just extremely difficult. We were assigned to basically read a book per week which doesn't seem like a lot but with all other work it gets hard. His class is 100% discussion based, and if you don't read the books you're screwed for the final

I loved this course. It was lecture heavy on occasion but mostly revolved around in class discussion. Russell was very flexible with deadlines and super accessible outside of class. The two major papers were challenging, but he was readily available for feedback at any point in the writing process. I highly recommend.

Russell is one of the worst professors I've ever had. Expect to read an entire book every week, 5 page analysis every week, and watch 1/2 movies almost every week. He is by far the hardest grader I've ever had and it is difficult, even impossible to do well across his essays. Do not recommend, as getting a B was close to impossible.

I guess he read these reviews since now he encourages questions, differing ideas/perspectives, and is a fair grader. He is very nice and energetic. His classes mostly consist of discussing about the books we have to read. BTW you don't need to buy any of the Shakespeare books. Just get it on spark notes- its the same thing, and he doesn't mind

I tried to like Prof. Russell at first, but he makes it really hard. He is incredibly condescending and made me not want to major in English. No matter how hard I worked, I received B's on my essays; this course killed my GPA.

Dr. Russell is hot, but that's all he has going for him. He's a pompous ass when it comes to Shakespeare, and if you don't agree with him on the text, he will ignore you. I offered an alternative view to one of Shakespeare's plays and he ignored me for the rest of class. Dare to be different in his class, and you'll fail. Hard.

Russell is what you see as the classical Italian cat: smooth, well-versed, and friendly. His specialty is Shakespeare, and he lives up to it. The only trouble is that you have to play his game to do well in his class (as with most professors). That means listen closely, and prepare to repeat his ideas in his papers/discussions.
Rennaissance poetry- Dr. Russell really knows his subject, but is difficult to engage outside of class. Always seemed more concerned with the poem, than actually TEACHING you about the poem.

Renn professor. Extraordinary lectures but appears irritated by questions and dislikes breaks when students raise a hand during the lecture. Difficult material being covered by an expert with high apptitude but is not accessible outside of class.
You can tell he really enjoys teaching. I'd sign up for another one of his classes.
great guy- enthusiastic, smart, and caring.

He's only interested in hearing his own thoughts regurgitated to him by the students in the class who are eager enough to do so. He works in direct contradiction to encouraging free discussion and equips students only with the ability to rephrase his own thoughts. I heard great things about him before I signed up, but was incredibly disappointed.

He's a nice man, really, but his critical style (marxist-materialist, horribly postmodern) does NOT motivate you -- it's like violently killing shakespeare himself, to read a shakespeare play with russell and have to listen to him tell you that the whole thing is "a theatricalization...of the spaces...of power...right..." instead of, like, ART.

Prof. Russell is an asset to the University. He motivated me to pursue a graduate degree from a very prestigious institution in the field of Renaissance Lit. He is demanding and pushes you to become a better scholar.
Don't let his surname fool you, this cat can parlare with the best of them.  Taught my section of 101 back in the late 1990's.  He's aight.  Forza Italia!
No Comments

really hot.  Wholly unhelpful and terrible in guiding discussion or motivating students.  He's lucky he's such a stud or no one would ever come to class.  His class made me dislike a subject I had been extremely interested in... but damn, he's hot.

He is a BRILLIANT man- extremely articulate, thoughtful, insightful, and really knows his Renaissance lit. Take his Renaissance Art and Letters of Faith class if you can; you won't regret it. He team teaches it with Dr. Charles Johnson who is also brilliant (although a little less animated).
he is sketchy.  very unhelpful and does not grade work consistently

I could listen to him read Shakespeare or Dante all day. He brings discussion above the level that UR discussions normally are, yet he brings the students along with him. If you've done your reading, you'll be able to follow.
Best professor I ever had.  Hard as hell, but you'll learn a ton.
awesome teacher, take his shakespeare class!
Awesome Shakespeare professor.  Take him if you can, he makes it very interesting.
